### • 5. Summarizing Data: Code {.unnumbered #summarizing_data_script}




### Overview

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| column: margin
#| fig-alt: "The R logo"
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(DT)
library(webexercises)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
source("../../_common.R") 
include_graphics("https://www.r-project.org/Rlogo.png")
```

Here I provide simple R code to generate the most common univariate data summaries.  Note the steps:

1. **Load packages.** See the [section loading data](#loading_data) from chapter three.  
2. **Load data.**   See the [section on packages](#packages) from chapter one.  
3. **Format data.** See the [chapter four](#data_in_R) for more info.    
   - Here I removed all `NA` data before analyzing. If you do not remove NA data before summarizing, be sure to include `na.rm=TRUE`. e.g. `mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)`.  
4. **Visualize data.** See the [section on visualizing a continuous variable](#one_continuous) from chapter two, and the sections on [summarizing shape](#summarizing_shape), and [summarizing variability](#summarizing_variability), from this chapter.  
5. **Summarize data**
   - Appropriate summaries depend on the [shape of the data](#summarizing_shape). Here I present all standard summaries of the ["average"](#summarizing_center) and the [variability](#summarizing_variability), but note that the left skew makes these somewhat difficult to interpret. 

---

```{r}
#| eval: false
###--------------------------
### Load Packages
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)


###--------------------------
### Load data
ril_link <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ybrandvain/datasets/refs/heads/master/clarkia_rils.csv"
ril_data <- readr::read_csv(ril_link)

###--------------------------
### Format data
gc_visits <- ril_data            |> 
  select(location, mean_visits)  |>   # Focus on two columns of interest
  rename(visits = mean_visits)   |>   # "mean visits" confuses me because it was mean per plant, so let's call it visits
  filter(location == "GC",            # let's focus on plants at GC 
         !is.na(visits))                  # with non-na-visits

###--------------------------
### Visualize before you summarize
# Boxplot
ggplot(gc_visits, aes(x = location, y = visits))+
  geom_boxplot()

# histogram
ggplot(gc_visits, aes(x = visits))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.15, color = "white")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| column: margin
#| fig-height: 8
###--------------------------
### Load Packages
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

###--------------------------
### Load data
ril_link <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ybrandvain/datasets/refs/heads/master/clarkia_rils.csv"
ril_data <- readr::read_csv(ril_link)

###--------------------------
### Format data
gc_visits <- ril_data            |> 
  select(location, mean_visits)  |>   # Focus on two columns of interest
  rename(visits = mean_visits)   |>   # "mean visits" confuses me because it was mean per plant, so let's call it visits
  filter(location == "GC",            # let's focus on plants at GC 
         !is.na(visits))                  # with non-na-visits

###--------------------------
### Visualize before you summarize
# Boxplot
a<-ggplot(gc_visits, aes(x = location, y = visits))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size=30),
        axis.text = element_text(size=25))

# histogram
b<-ggplot(gc_visits, aes(x = visits))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.15, color = "white") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size=30),
        axis.text = element_text(size=25))

a / b + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A')
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| fig-cap: "Two displays of the number of visitors per RIL platn at GC. (A) A boxplot  showing the number of visits recorded per observation at the GC site. Most observations are zero (that's why the box is so small), with a few higher values. (B) Histogram of visits at the GC site, illustrating a strongly right-skewed distribution with a large spike at zero and a long tail of rare higher counts."
#| fig-alt: "Two-panel figure labeled A and B. Panel A shows a box plot of visits at the GC location, with most points at zero and a few scattered up to about two visits. Panel B shows a histogram of visits with a very tall bar at zero and progressively smaller bars toward higher visit values, indicating a highly right-skewed distribution."
#| label: fig-pic
# The plots show highly right skewed data - most plants 
#   receive zero or few visits, some receive many
# I will continue with the standard run of summaries, 
#   but note, some are less appropriate for this shape

###--------------------------
### Data summaries

## Summarizing center
gc_visits |>
  summarise(mean_visits   = mean(visits),                # Mean
            median_visits = median(visits))              # Median

## Summarizing variability
gc_visits |>
  summarise(iqr_visits    = IQR(visits),                 # Interquartile range
            sd_visits     = sd(visits),                  # Standard deviation
            var_visits    = var(visits),                 # Variance
            coef_var_visits = sd(visits) / mean(visits)) # Coefficient of variation
```


```{r}
#| echo: false
# The plots show highly right skewed data - most plants 
#   receive zero or few visits, some receive many
# I will continue with the standard run of summaries, 
#   but note, some are less appropriate for this shape

###--------------------------
### Data summaries

## Summarizing center
a <- gc_visits |>
  summarise(mean_visits   = mean(visits),                # Center: Mean
            median_visits = median(visits))              # Center: Median

## Summarizing center
b<- gc_visits |>
  summarise(iqr_visits    = IQR(visits),
            sd_visits     = sd(visits),
            var_visits    = var(visits),
            coef_var_visits = sd(visits) / mean(visits)) 

a |>
  mutate_all(round, digits = 4)|>
  kbl(caption = "Summarizing the average pollinator visits at GC") |>
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria")

b |>
  mutate_all(round, digits = 4)|>
  kbl(caption = "Summarizing variability in pollinator visits at GC") |>
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria")
```
